extracted.intended_audience: immigration applicants, attorneys, accredited representatives, and USCIS adjudicators
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and evidentiary requirements for filing and adjudicating Applications for T Nonimmigrant Status (including derivatives) and related rules for U- and V- classification referenced in this chunk. Focuses on eligibility elements, required evidence, filing/jurisdiction, periods of admission, extensions, revocation, and procedural effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial evidence for Form I-918, Supplement A
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-918, Supplement A, must include evidence demonstrating the relationship of a qualifying family member, as provided in paragraph (f)(4) of this section; and if the qualifying family member is inadmissible, Form I-192, 'Application for Advance Permission to Enter as a Non-Immigrant,' in accordance with 8 CFR 212.17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplement A must show the qualifying relationship; submit Form I-192 if inadmissible. (See paragraph (f)(3)(i)-(ii).)

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of relationship for qualifying family members (U Supplement A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as set forth in paragraphs (f)(4)(i) and (ii), the relationship between the U-1 principal alien and the qualifying family member must exist at the time Form I-918 was filed, and the relationship must continue to exist at the time Form I-918, Supplement A is adjudicated, and at the time of the qualifying family member's subsequent admission to the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relationship must be established at filing and persist through adjudication and admission; otherwise Supplement A may not be approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — child born after Form I-918 filing (U Supplement A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the U-1 principal alien proves that he or she has become the parent of a child after Form I-918 was filed, the child shall be eligible to accompany or follow to join the U-1 principal alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Birth of a child to the principal after filing qualifies that child as a family member eligible to accompany/follow to join.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — sibling filed when principal under 21 (U Supplement A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the principal alien was under 21 years of age at the time he or she filed Form I-918, and filed Form I-918, Supplement A for an unmarried sibling under the age of 18, USCIS will continue to consider such sibling as a qualifying family member for purposes of U nonimmigrant status even if the principal alien is no longer under 21 years of age at the time of adjudication, and even if the sibling is no longer under 18 years of age at the time of adjudication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects juvenile-sibling derivative eligibility when principal's or sibling's ages change between filing and adjudication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biometric capture and evidentiary standards applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions for biometric capture and evidentiary standards in paragraphs (c)(3) and (c)(4) of this section also are applicable to petitions for qualifying family members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the same biometric and evidence collection standards applied to principal petitions when filing for qualifying family members.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS decision and notifications for Form I-918, Supplement A
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will issue a written decision approving or denying Form I-918, Supplement A and send notice of this decision to the U-1 principal petitioner. USCIS will include in a decision approving Form I-918 a list of nongovernmental organizations to which the qualifying family member can refer regarding his or her options while in the United States and available resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approvals or denials are provided in writing to the principal; approvals include NGO resource referrals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic cancellation of DHS orders upon USCIS approval (U Supplement A)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a qualifying family member who is subject to an order of exclusion, deportation, or removal issued by the Secretary, the order will be deemed canceled by operation of law as of the date of USCIS' approval of Form I-918, Supplement A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval cancels DHS-issued exclusion/deportation/removal orders automatically as of approval date; orders by IJ/Board require motion to reopen/terminate removal proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for qualifying family members who had IJ/Board orders
rubrics_metrics.description: A qualifying family member who is subject to an order of exclusion, deportation, or removal issued by an immigration judge or the Board may seek cancellation of such order by filing, with the immigration judge or the Board, a motion to reopen and terminate removal proceedings. ICE counsel may agree, as a matter of discretion, to join such a motion to overcome any applicable time and numerical limitations of 8 CFR 1003.2 and 1003.23.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior order is from an IJ/Board, the individual must move to reopen/terminate proceedings; ICE discretion may be used to join the motion in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approvals for qualifying family members within the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: When USCIS approves a Form I-918, Supplement A for a qualifying family member who is within the United States, it will concurrently grant that alien U-2, U-3, U-4, or U-5 nonimmigrant status and notify the principal on Form I-797 with Form I-94 indicating U classification. Aliens previously granted U interim relief will be accorded U nonimmigrant status as of the date that the request for U interim relief was approved. Aliens granted U-2, U-3, U-4, or U-5 nonimmigrant status are not subject to an annual numerical limit. USCIS may not approve Supplement A unless it has approved the principal alien's Form I-918.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent grant of derivative U status and Form I-94/I-797 notification; principal's Form I-918 approval is prerequisite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approvals for qualifying family members outside the United States
rubrics_metrics.description: When USCIS approves Form I-918, Supplement A for a qualifying family member who is outside the United States, USCIS will notify the principal on Form I-797 and forward the approved Supplement A to the Department of State for delivery to the U.S. Embassy/Consulate or to the appropriate port of entry for visa-exempt aliens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External-derivative approvals are transmitted to DOS for visa issuance or port-of-entry processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial of Form I-918, Supplement A — notice and appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will provide written notification of the reasons for the denial in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3(a)(1). The principal alien may appeal the denial to the Administrative Appeals Office in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3. Upon USCIS' final denial for a qualifying family member who was in removal proceedings terminated pursuant to 8 CFR 214.14(f)(2)(i), DHS may file a new Notice to Appear to place the individual in proceedings again. Denial will lift any stay of removal as of the date the denial becomes administratively final for family members subject to an order of removal, deportation, or exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Denials must state reasons; AAO appeals available per 8 CFR 103.3; final denials can re-trigger removal processes and lift stays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment authorization for U derivative nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien granted U-2, U-3, U-4, or U-5 nonimmigrant status is employment authorized incident to status. To obtain an EAD, such alien must file Form I-765 with the appropriate fee or a request for a fee waiver in accordance with form instructions. For qualifying family members within the United States, Form I-765 may be filed concurrently with Form I-918, Supplement A, or at any time thereafter. For qualifying family members outside the United States, Form I-765 may only be filed after admission to the United States in U nonimmigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EAD application mechanics: concurrent filing allowed only for in-U.S. derivatives; outside-U.S. derivatives must wait until admission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of U nonimmigrant status (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: U nonimmigrant status may be approved for a period not to exceed 4 years in the aggregate. A qualifying family member's initial period will not exceed the expiration date of the initial period approved for the principal alien.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aggregate cap of 4 years; derivative duration tied to principal's initial period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of U nonimmigrant status — Form I-539
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a U nonimmigrant's approved period of stay on Form I-94 is less than 4 years, he or she may file Form I-539 to request an extension of U status for an aggregate period not to exceed 4 years. USCIS may approve an extension for a qualifying family member beyond the date when the U-1's status expires when delays in consular processing prevent timely entry and an extension is necessary to ensure the qualifying family member attains at least 3 years in nonimmigrant status for adjustment purposes under section 245(m) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Form I-539 for extensions up to the 4-year cap; consular delay can justify extension to meet 3-year adjustment requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension beyond 4 years — certifying official attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of U nonimmigrant status beyond the 4-year period are available upon attestation by the certifying official that the alien's presence in the United States continues to be necessary to assist in the investigation or prosecution of qualifying criminal activity. To obtain such an extension, the alien must file Form I-539 and a newly executed Form I-918, Supplement B in accordance with the Form I-539 instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extraordinary extensions require certifying official attestation and new Supplement B plus Form I-539 filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automatic revocation of approved U-1 petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An approved petition for U-1 nonimmigrant status will be revoked automatically if, pursuant to 8 CFR 214.14(d)(1), the beneficiary notifies the USCIS office that approved the petition that he or she will not apply for admission to the United States and, therefore, the petition will not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beneficiary's written notice of non-use triggers automatic revocation; automatic revocations cannot be appealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revocation on notice — grounds (U petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may revoke an approved petition for U nonimmigrant status following a notice of intent to revoke based on one or more of: (A) certifying official withdraws or disavows certification; (B) approval was in error; (C) fraud in the petition; (D) termination of relationship to principal (for U-2..); or (E) principal U-1's nonimmigrant status is revoked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocation for specified grounds; USCIS issues Notice of Intent to Revoke with stated grounds and rebuttal period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of intent to revoke — procedural protections
rubrics_metrics.description: The notice of intent to revoke must be in writing, contain the grounds for revocation and the time period allowed for the U nonimmigrant's rebuttal. The alien may submit evidence in rebuttal within 30 days of the notice. USCIS shall consider all relevant evidence presented; determination of relevance and weight is within USCIS' sole discretion. If revoked, USCIS will provide a written notice explaining specific reasons for the revocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 30-day rebuttal period; discretionary weighing of evidence by USCIS; written explanation on revocation if finalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appealability of revocations
rubrics_metrics.description: A revocation on notice may be appealed to the Administrative Appeals Office in accordance with 8 CFR 103.3 within 30 days after the date of the notice. Automatic revocations may not be appealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish automatic vs on-notice revocations for appeal rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of revocation on principal and derivatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Revocation of a principal alien's approved Form I-918 will result in termination of status for the principal alien and denial of any pending Supplement A filed for qualifying family members. Revocation of a qualifying family member's approved Supplement A will result in termination of status for that family member. Revocation of an approved Form I-918 or Supplement A also revokes any waiver of inadmissibility granted with the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revocations cascade to derivatives and nullify related inadmissibility waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS ability to institute removal proceedings after admission or revocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing prohibits USCIS from instituting removal proceedings under section 240 of the Act for conduct committed after admission, conduct/conditions not disclosed to USCIS prior to granting U status, misrepresentations of material facts in Form I-918 or Supplement A and supporting documentation, or after revocation of U nonimmigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjudication of U status does not shield against later removal where new facts or misrepresentation are discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: V nonimmigrant eligibility — filing/pending petition timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien who is the beneficiary of an immigrant visa petition to accord a status under section 203(a)(2)(A) filed on or before December 21, 2000, may apply for V status if: (1) such immigrant petition has been pending for 3 years or more; or (2) such petition has been approved and 3 or more years have passed since such filing date when either an immigrant visa is not immediately available due to waiting list or the alien's immigrant visa/adjustment application remains pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is tied to very specific filing-date and pendency/approval + 3-year rules (pre-12/21/2000 filings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'pending petition' for V status
rubrics_metrics.description: A pending petition is one filed with USCIS under section 204 on or before Dec 21, 2000, not adjudicated, properly filed per 8 CFR 103.2(a). If USCIS returns the petition for any reason or issues a request for evidence or notice of intent to deny, the petitioner must comply within the time set. If USCIS denies but appeal is pending, the petition is considered pending until administrative appeal decided. A petition rejected as not properly filed is not pending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper filing and compliance with RFEs, and appeals preserve 'pending' status; rejected petitions do not count as pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: V nonimmigrant application contents (in U.S.)
rubrics_metrics.description: To apply for V status in the United States, an eligible alien must submit: (i) Form I-539 with required fee; (ii) the fingerprint fee as required; (iii) Form I-693 (medical exam) without vaccination supplement; and (iv) evidence of eligibility as described by Supplement A and paragraph (f)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow Supplement A instructions for evidence; include required fees and medical examination documentation (no vaccination supplement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable evidence for V application
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof of filing of the immigrant petition may include Form I-797 (receipt or approval), a receipt or notice issued by a local district office, or other correspondence to/from the Service regarding a pending petition. If none of these exist, the applicant should state where/when the petition was filed, petitioner's name and alien number, and names of beneficiaries if known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If standard proof unavailable, provide a detailed sworn statement describing where/when petition was filed and identifying petitioner/beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Period of admission for V nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: V-1 spouses will be granted a period of admission not to exceed 2 years. V-2/V-3 children will be granted up to 2 years or until the day before their 21st birthday, whichever comes first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ordinary admission periods capped at 2 years; child derivative limited by age.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of V status and timing to apply
rubrics_metrics.description: Aliens may apply for extension of V status by filing Form I-539 and the filing fee on or before 120 days before expiration. If approved, extension granted for up to 2 years or in case of a child until the day before the 21st birthday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely filing (120 days) recommended for extensions; extension durations mirror initial limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules for aliens with current priority date but no pending immigrant visa abroad
rubrics_metrics.description: An otherwise eligible alien applying at a Port-of-Entry with a current priority date but no pending immigrant visa abroad will be admitted for a 6-month period (or until day before 21st birthday). Such an alien in the U.S. applying for extension will receive a one-time extension not to exceed 6 months. If no adjustment/immigrant visa application is filed within that 6-month period, the alien cannot extend or be admitted/readmitted to V status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited 6-month admission/extension windows apply to certain priority-date holders; filing for adjustment or immigrant visa within the 6 months is required to remain eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: V nonimmigrant employment authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien in V status may apply for employment authorization by filing Form I-765 with the fee required by 8 CFR 103.7. Employment authorization will be granted for a period equal to the alien's authorized admission as a V nonimmigrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EAD validity mirrors period of authorized V admission; follow Form I-765 instructions and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and readmission rules for V nonimmigrants
rubrics_metrics.description: Form I-797 indicating V status does not serve as a travel document. If a V-status alien departs the U.S., they must obtain a V visa at a consular office abroad to be readmitted, except for certain cases (travel to contiguous territory/adjacent islands, another valid visa, or eligibility for automatic revalidation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on Form I-797 for reentry; plan consular visa issuance or rely on narrow automatic revalidation exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: V nonimmigrant effect of unlawful presence on adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: A V nonimmigrant is not subject to inadmissibility under section 212(a)(9)(B) when applying for admission as a V nonimmigrant (even with >180 days unlawful presence). However, when applying for immigrant visa or adjustment of status, the alien is subject to 212(a)(9)(B); departure after >180 days unlawful presence will render the alien inadmissible for adjustment unless a waiver under 212(a)(9)(B)(v) is obtained or an exception applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonimmigrant admission may be allowed despite unlawful presence, but adjustment/admission as an immigrant is still subject to unlawful presence bars unless waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination triggers for V nonimmigrant status
rubrics_metrics.description: V nonimmigrant status automatically terminates 30 days following occurrence of: denial/withdrawal/revocation of the Form I-130 filed on behalf of that alien; denial/withdrawal of the immigrant visa application; denial/withdrawal of adjustment application; the V-1 spouse's divorce becoming final; or marriage of an alien in V-2 or V-3 status. When principal's V status terminates, v-dependent or derivative status terminates as well.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status termination is automatic 30 days after listed events; derivative status follows principal's termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals delay termination for V status
rubrics_metrics.description: If the denial of the immigrant visa petition is appealed, the alien's V nonimmigrant status does not terminate until 30 days after the administrative appeal is dismissed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing and pendency of appeals can temporarily preserve V status beyond initial denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate initiation of removal for V status violations
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing precludes the Service from immediately initiating removal proceedings for other violations of an alien's V nonimmigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with status conditions is required to avoid removal regardless of V status protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of petitioner naturalization on V status
rubrics_metrics.description: If the LPR who filed the qualifying I-130 subsequently naturalizes, the V nonimmigrant status of the spouse and children will terminate after their current period of admission ends. However, they will be considered immediate relatives of a U.S. citizen and immediately eligible to apply for adjustment of status and related employment authorization. If they already filed I-485 prior to naturalization, a new application is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Naturalization ends V status prospectively but creates immediate-relative adjustment eligibility; prior-filed I-485s continue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative closure for aliens in proceedings seeking V status
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien in immigration proceedings who believes they may be eligible for V status should request administrative closure (or indefinite continuance of a motion) to pursue V application with the Service. If the Service finds the alien eligible, it can adjudicate the change of status; if ineligible, the Service will recommence proceedings by filing a motion to re-calendar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request administrative closure from IJ/Board to allow V application process; Service adjudication determines next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart C — T nonimmigrant status applications
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart governs the submission and adjudication of an Application for T Nonimmigrant Status, including requests by a principal applicant on behalf of eligible family members for derivative status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All T application filing and adjudication rules for principals and derivatives are governed by this subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'severe form of trafficking in persons'
rubrics_metrics.description: Severe form of trafficking in persons means sex trafficking in which a commercial sex act is induced by force, fraud, or coercion, or involving a person under 18; or recruitment/harboring/transportation/provision/obtaining of a person for labor or services through force, fraud, or coercion for purposes of involuntary servitude, peonage, debt bondage, or slavery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key statutory definition used to determine whether an applicant is a trafficking victim under the TVPA/Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'serious harm'
rubrics_metrics.description: Serious harm means any harm, whether physical or nonphysical, including psychological, financial, or reputational harm, that is sufficiently serious, under all surrounding circumstances, to compel a reasonable person of the same background and in the same circumstances to perform or continue performing labor or services to avoid incurring that harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in assessing coercion, involuntary servitude, and hardship; includes nonphysical harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'coercion' for T purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Coercion means threats of serious harm or physical restraint; any scheme, plan, or pattern intended to cause a person to believe failure to perform an act would result in serious harm or physical restraint; or the abuse/threatened abuse of the legal process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition that covers psychological and legal coercion; central to commercial-sex and labor-trafficking determinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'involuntary servitude' and 'peonage' and 'debt bondage'
rubrics_metrics.description: Involuntary servitude means servitude induced by schemes/patterns causing belief in serious harm or legal coercion, and includes conditions where victims are forced to work by threat/use of physical restraint or coercion; peonage is servitude based on indebtedness; debt bondage is debtor's pledge of personal services as security where services' value isn't applied to debt liquidation and length/nature of services aren't limited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions delineate labor-trafficking modalities used to assess victimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — Law Enforcement Agency (LEA) and LEA declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: LEA means a federal, state, tribal, or local law enforcement agency, prosecutor, judge, labor agency, children's protective services agency, adult protective services agency, or other authority responsible for detection/investigation/prosecution of severe trafficking. An LEA declaration is an official LEA declaration submitted on the Declaration for Trafficking Victim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEA involvement and declarations are used as evidence of victimization and cooperation with law enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'law enforcement involvement' for physical presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Law enforcement involvement, for purposes of establishing physical presence, means law enforcement action beyond receiving the applicant's reporting and may include the LEA interviewing the applicant or otherwise becoming involved in detecting, investigating, or prosecuting the acts of trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical presence evidence may include documentation of substantive LEA involvement, not merely a report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'request for assistance' and its reasonableness standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Request for assistance means a request by an LEA to a victim to assist in detection, investigation, or prosecution of trafficking or of a crime where trafficking is at least one central reason. The reasonableness of the request is assessed using factors delineated at § 214.208(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an applicant complied with LEA assistance is judged by a reasonableness test set out elsewhere (§ 214.208(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: T-1 eligibility element: Victim of a severe form of trafficking
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is or has been a victim of a severe form of trafficking in persons, according to § 214.206.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must establish victimization per statutory/regulatory definitions; see supporting standards in § 214.206.

rubrics_metrics.name: T-1 eligibility element: Physical presence in U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant is physically present in the United States, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, or at a port-of-entry thereto, according to § 214.207.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical presence in one of the enumerated jurisdictions is required for T-1 eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: T-1 eligibility element: Compliance with any reasonable request for assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has complied with any reasonable request for assistance from law enforcement or meets one of the exceptions (minor victims under 18 or inability to cooperate due to trauma). The reasonableness of the request is assessed using factors in § 214.208(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants under 18 or those unable to cooperate due to trauma are exempt; otherwise, cooperation or explanation required and assessed under § 214.208(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: T-1 eligibility element: Hardship (extreme hardship upon removal)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant would suffer extreme hardship involving unusual and severe harm upon removal, according to § 214.209.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must demonstrate extreme, unusual, and severe harm that would result from removal; § 214.209 explains standards and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: T-1 ineligibility — trafficker prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: No applicant will be eligible to receive T nonimmigrant status if there is substantial reason to believe that the applicant has committed an act of a severe form of trafficking in persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspected traffickers are barred from T status.

rubrics_metrics.name: T-1 and derivative period of admission
rubrics_metrics.description: T-1 nonimmigrant status may be approved for a period not to exceed 4 years (except as provided in section 214(o)(7)). A derivative family member may be granted T-2 through T-6 status for an initial period not to exceed the expiration date of the T-1 principal's initial period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard initial period up to 4 years; derivative duration tied to principal's period.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS jurisdiction over T applications
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS has sole jurisdiction over all applications for T nonimmigrant status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All T filings and adjudications go to USCIS, not to consular posts or immigration courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing rules for applicants in removal or prior deportation orders
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant in removal proceedings or subject to a final order of removal, deportation, or exclusion may file an Application for T Nonimmigrant Status directly with USCIS. Filing has no effect on DHS authority to execute a final order, although the applicant may request an administrative stay of removal. If the applicant is in detention pending execution of a final order, the period of detention will be extended while a stay is in effect. If USCIS subsequently determines the application bona fide, the final order will be automatically stayed until final decision on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants with proceedings/final orders can still file with USCIS; stay relief and detention extensions are possible while USCIS adjudicates bona fides.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS discretion not to refer for removal proceedings while T application pending
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS generally will not refer a T applicant for removal proceedings while the application is pending or following denial, absent serious aggravating circumstances such as egregious criminal history, national security threat, or applicant complicit in trafficking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referral to immigration court is exceptional and tied to severe aggravating factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: USCIS handling of minor T applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: When USCIS receives an application from a principal applicant under 18, USCIS will notify the Department of Health and Human Services to facilitate provision of interim assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS notification triggers services for minor applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: T application — required initial evidence (personal statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Application for T Nonimmigrant Status must include a detailed, signed personal statement from the applicant, in their own words, addressing: the circumstances surrounding victimization (nature, timing, duration, escape/rescue/separation, events, who was responsible, circumstances of entry to U.S. if related to trafficking); how physical presence in the U.S. relates to the trafficking; the hardship (harm or mistreatment feared if removed); and whether they complied with reasonable law enforcement requests and whether any criminal/civil/administrative records relating to the acts of trafficking exist (or if applicable, why the age exemption or trauma exception applies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal statement should be detailed and cover each enumerated subpart; it is primary evidence of circumstances and should be signed and in applicant's own words.

rubrics_metrics.name: T application — supporting credible evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Any credible evidence that supports any of the eligibility requirements set out in §§ 214.206 through 214.209 should be submitted with the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corroborative evidence may include medical records, police reports, affidavits, declarations, photographs, records of removal/escape, or other relevant documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadmissible T applicants — waiver for inadmissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant is inadmissible to the United States, they must submit a request for a waiver of inadmissibility on the Application for Advance Permission to Enter as a Nonimmigrant (or successor form) in accordance with form instructions and 8 CFR 212.16, accompanied by supporting evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inadmissibility does not automatically bar filing but requires a formal waiver request and supporting documentation per form instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of LEA evidence for T applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may submit evidence from a law enforcement agency to help establish eligibility, including victimization and compliance with reasonable requests for assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LEA declarations, investigative reports, or official correspondence can strongly support victimization and cooperation elements.
